items.headline: Microsoft and Alphabet both report AI capex below Wall Street estimates: $45.2B vs $50.7B expected, and $51.4B vs $55.1B expected
items.why: Slower-than-planned data-center spend, which Microsoft blamed on delayed third-party capacity, puts the revenue ramps of the outside AI-cloud providers it buys from in question, and AI-cloud stocks fell on the day.

sources.title: AI Cloud Stocks Fall as Big Tech Capex Comes in Light - 24/7 Wall St.

items.headline: Intel falls about 29% in its worst day since 1974 after guiding Q4 revenue to $15-16B against $17.1B expected
items.why: A guided gross-margin drop to 38% from 44.1% and a PC slowdown management expects to last into the first half of 2027 outweighed 78% growth in data-center and AI revenue.

items.headline: Amazon's AWS grows 39% but trailing-twelve-month free cash flow turns to a $42.4B outflow on AI investment
items.why: Cloud growth is strong, yet the cost of funding it is now visible in free cash flow, which is the concern behind the AI-spending selloff.

items.why: The $76,000 area held on two consecutive days, and the Fear and Greed Index dropped to 30 from 51 two days earlier, so the level to watch is whether it holds.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters favoring a hike; markets price roughly 75% odds of a December increase
items.why: Strong Q3 GDP and energy-driven inflation have moved the debate from cuts to whether tightening continues, which is repricing every rate-sensitive asset.

items.why: Supply risk through Hormuz is feeding the oil move that keeps central banks hawkish, so this is the live link between the Iran conflict and rate expectations.
